title: Segregated seating, Ellington's band and Woody Herman at the Hyatt
summary: He recalls the seating reversal at the concert, the Paradise Restaurant in New York, and says Woody Herman's band was closest to Ellington's.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: He was, it was a great, it was a great band and we were very close and then they went away but nothing happened. I mean, I'll tell you, I was so afraid somebody was going to see me with a nigger walking around with his arm around my shoulder but Sonny, when I told Sonny, my father died, he absolutely cried because even when Duke Ellington used to come down to the auditorium, oh, I got to tell you this, when I went back to my seat, the five dollar seats, thinking there were going to be all rich, white people sitting in the five dollar seats, the white people, rich people were sitting in the two dollar seats in the back and all of them in the front was all black. They got the five dollar seats but Juan Tizzo was a trombone player and they were all a beautiful bunch of guys. Well, you see, we were down at Jack Dempsey's and they were playing up at the Paradise Restaurant right above us. It was right on the second floor above Jack Dempsey's in the Brill Building. And uh, no it wasn't the Brill Building, it was down, right next to the Brill Building. But uh, the Duke was a gentleman, he was a real gentleman, this guy. And uh, the guys, all the guys were gentlemen. There was nothing wrong with them. And uh, Duke's band, Duke's band was, and his son took over the band and it was nothing like what it used to be. The closest thing to Duke Ellington's band that I have ever heard, I mean Duke Ellington's good band, that I ever heard, was when Woody Herman was down here at the Hyatt Regency Hotel. He had a hell of a band down here. And there was only one trouble with it. It was too good and it was too loud and the damn women didn't understand it, cause my own wife, they had a whole Dixieland band there, with half-assed musicians playing and playing not too loud. I said, which one did you like? Oh, I like the Dixieland band better. I said, why? She said, the other band was too loud, couldn't appreciate it. But I mean, that band that they had down here, he had about five trumpet players with him. And Woody had one hell of a band down here at the, did you get a chance to hear him with the Hyatt Regency down there? Yeah. What was your opinion of it? Well, I thought it was, he had a good
band, but they were a little inconsistent, depending, you know, if you caught him on a good night. That's probably a good night. I thought it was a good night evidently. But I mean, it was, it was
